## Feature Importance by Horizon


```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 100%
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-height: 100%
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import plotly.graph_objects as go


avg_imp_df = pd.read_csv("results/feature_importance_by_horizon_rf.csv")



# Example expected columns:
# avg_imp_df.columns -> ['feature', 'importance', 'horizon']

# Optional: keep only top N features within each horizon
top_n = 25
plot_df = (
    avg_imp_df
    .sort_values(['horizon', 'importance'], ascending=[True, False])
    .groupby('horizon')
    .head(top_n)
    .copy()
)

horizons = sorted(plot_df['horizon'].unique())

fig = go.Figure()

for i, h in enumerate(horizons):
    df_h = (
        plot_df[plot_df['horizon'] == h]
        .sort_values('importance', ascending=True)  # ascending for nicer horizontal bars
    )

    fig.add_trace(
        go.Bar(
            x=df_h['importance'],
            y=df_h['feature'],
            orientation='h',
            name=f'Horizon {h}',
            visible=(i == 0)
        )
    )

buttons = []
for i, h in enumerate(horizons):
    visible = [False] * len(horizons)
    visible[i] = True

    buttons.append(
        dict(
            label=f'Horizon {h}',
            method='update',
            args=[
                {'visible': visible},
                {'title': f'Feature importance - Horizon {h}'}
            ]
        )
    )

fig.update_layout(
    title=f'Feature importance - Horizon {horizons[0]}',
    updatemenus=[
        dict(
            buttons=buttons,
            direction='down',
            showactive=True,
            x=1.02,
            xanchor='left',
            y=1,
            yanchor='top'
        )
    ],
    xaxis_title='Importance',
    yaxis_title='Feature',
    height=700,
    template='plotly_white',
    margin=dict(l=100, r=40, t=80, b=40)
)

fig.show()

```
